result.summary:
Scope test: real behavioral surface (two scheduled jobs, three handlers writing real feedback/users rows) -- full Steps 3b/4 apply, not the docs-only skip. Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-031.md designing two new vitest files (neither exists yet -- BACKEND-DEV's step-02 handoff committed no test file, artifacts_out lists only schema/domain/handler/scheduler/i18n/index.ts files):

1. apps/bot/src/scheduler/feedbackJobs.db.test.ts (job-level, modeled on reminderJobs.db.test.ts's own shape -- real Postgres, makeFakeSender, explicit evaluationTime, never the wall clock): AC1 (checked-in registration receives the T+2h request via an exact sent.length===1 assertion; a second, admitted-but-never-checked-in registration seeded in the SAME test never appears -- checked_in_at IS NOT NULL is the mechanism the exact-count assertion catches a regression to); AC7 piggybacked onto the same AC1 fixture (the checked-in registrant's own broadcastOptIn is explicitly set false, and the send still happens -- proving the transactional classification ignores it, with a documented failure mode: a future reclassification to "marketing" would silently start filtering this exact fixture out); AC4 (three runs -- T+24h genuine send, an immediate same-evaluationTime re-run proving the REQ-025 ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id,kind) dedup directly, and a T+48h re-run whose zero-candidate outcome is traced through the actual CATCH_UP_WINDOW_MS arithmetic read from the source rather than assumed -- total sends across all three runs asserted exactly 1, the literal count-across-runs check the task required).

2. apps/bot/src/handlers/feedback.db.test.ts (dispatch-level, modeled on checkinQr.forgery.test.ts's own shape -- real grammY Bot, bot.api.config.use() capture, bot.handleUpdate(), never a hand-built Context): AC2 (full nps+liked+improve[skip]+topicVotes flow ending in exactly one feedback row, THEN a direct raw db.insert() duplicate-INSERT attempt bypassing writeFeedbackNps's own ON CONFLICT upsert entirely, asserted to reject with Postgres code 23505 -- AC2's own literal stated verification method, mirroring REQ-025's ledger-uniqueness test pattern per the task's own instruction); AC3 full-skip fixture (all three optional fields skipped, feedback row still saves with the correct skip-flag/null-value shape) PLUS a dedicated stale-reply field-match case: answers liked, captures that now-superseded prompt's exact text, then replies to THAT OLD prompt while the flow has already moved on to expecting improve -- asserts both liked and improve are byte-unchanged afterward AND that zero new Telegram messages were sent for that update (advanceFeedbackFlow never reached) -- this is the exact case the task named as the whole point of this design's rework, with an explicit failure-mode trace back to handlers/feedback.ts:267's three-clause gate; AC5 as two SEPARATE fixtures, one per answer value (decline and accept), each driving a second registration's flow to completion and asserting the broadcast-ask prompt is never re-sent AND that the stored boolean answer is unchanged either way -- the accept-case fixture is called out explicitly as the ONLY one of the two that can catch a regression gating on broadcastOptIn's own value instead of broadcastOptInAskedAt, per SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own flagged concern; AC6 as a static git grep (talk|speaker|want to speak, case-insensitive) across every file this requirement touched, zero matches expected; the S3 exploit case as three sub-attacks, one per handler (NPS callback, text-reply, broadcast callback), each seeding a second identity (Bob) who forges/reuses Alice's own registrationId and is refused with no write in every case, including a check that Bob's OWN feedback/user state is also left untouched by the refused attempt.

Claimed tg_id ranges (confirmed fresh via grep -rn "nextTgId = " apps/bot/src against every existing file's own range -- 800M/900M/920M/940M/941M/942M(x2, pre-existing ISS-0026 collision)/943M/950M/960M/970M/980M/990M/1000000900): 993_000_000+ for feedbackJobs.db.test.ts, 994_000_000+ for feedback.db.test.ts. No collision with any existing or previously-claimed range.

Every acceptance criterion (AC1-AC7) plus the S3 exploit case plus the stale-reply field-match case has at least one verification case in the spec that would fail if the property it targets were violated -- no case checks something trivial merely to have a case (e.g. AC1's admitted-but-never-checked-in registration is a real, seeded, would-otherwise-match fixture, not a no-op placeholder; the stale-reply case's two negative assertions -- liked unchanged AND improve unchanged -- each independently catch a different specific misattribution bug rather than one generic 'nothing happened' check).
